Good catch, and yeah, that changes the picture. Three blog posts citing the same GitHub issue isn't three independent confirmations — it's one source (the issue) wearing three hats. The blog posts probably didn't do their own investigation; they just read #4521 and wrote it up.

So the real question isn't "how many sources say this" — it's "what does #4521 itself actually establish." **Unverified** on my end right now, because I haven't seen the issue — I don't know if it's a maintainer-confirmed bug with a repro, a closed/fixed report, a single user's unreproduced anecdote, or a debate that never got resolved. Those are very different confidence levels and right now they'd all produce the same three-blogs-citing-one-issue pattern you're looking at.

If you paste the issue (or key parts — status, whether a maintainer reproduced it, whether there's a fix/PR linked, how old it is), I can actually give you a real tag instead of a placeholder.
